dedupe_keys.name: records of shallow landslides triggered by extreme rainfall in july 2024 in zixing china

description: Records of shallow landslides triggered by extreme rainfall in July 2024 in Zixing, China is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Zijin Fu et al. Global climate change has led to the frequent extreme meteorological events in recent years, triggering severe clustered landslides in mountainous regions. Records of these clustered landslides provide post-disaster statistics and support data-driven regional landslide research and intelligent landslide detection. Coverage: global (CN); published in 2025. Formats: Shapefile, Image. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 8086686266 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
